content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain the role of bacteria in nitrogen fixation and denitrification
Understand why nitrogen is important for organisms
Describe how humans affect the nitrogen cycle

describes how nitrogen moves through ecosystems. Despite nitrogen making up 78% of the atmosphere, most organisms cannot use it directly. Special bacteria convert nitrogen into usable forms, making the nitrogen cycle essential for all life.
Most organisms cannot use N₂ gas from atmosphere
Bacteria live in root nodules of legumes (peas, beans, clover)
Bacteria fix nitrogen → plant gets ammonium
Plant provides sugars → bacteria get energy
Absorption of nitrogen compounds by organisms
Get nitrogen from proteins in food
Proteins broken down to amino acids
Converting nitrates back to N₂ gas
Makes nitrogen available to all organisms
Balance can be disrupted by humans
Plants can use nitrogen gas from the air
Plants need nitrogen as nitrates or ammonium
All bacteria do the same thing in the cycle
The nitrogen cycle only involves soil
It includes atmosphere, organisms, and water
Swelling on legume roots containing bacteria
Nitrogen is essential for proteins and DNA

Nitrogen fixation: N₂ → NH₄⁺ (by nitrogen-fixing bacteria)
Plants absorb nitrates; animals get nitrogen from food
Denitrification: NO₃⁻ → N₂ (returns nitrogen to atmosphere)
Human activities can disrupt the cycle (fertilisers, eutrophication)
